{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Continuous positive-valued outcome with right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81), but large n=76655 provides robustness. Consider log-transformation or Welch's ANOVA if variance heterogeneity is severe.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1). Plain ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or equivalently, chi-squared test of independence. Report odds ratios relative to reference paradigm (e.g., Sham).",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Highly right-skewed (max=29.82, mean=0.47, min near 0). Strong violation of normality expected. Consider log-transformation, rank-based ANOVA (Kruskal-Wallis), or robust regression.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Moderate right skew (max=75.35, mean=12.50). Check variance homogeneity; consider Welch's ANOVA if needed.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Bounded [0,1] with mean=0.38, sd=0.24. Moderate skew toward lower values. Beta regression or arcsin-sqrt transformation may improve model fit, but standard ANOVA may be acceptable with large n."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed via experimental design; verify no temporal or spatial autocorrelation in residuals.",
    "Normality: Assess via Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals (or within-group residuals given large n). Expect violations for Path Efficiency and possibly Time-to-Target and Success.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for equality of variances across Stim Paradigm groups. Given unequal group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505), Welch's ANOVA or heteroskedasticity-consistent standard errors may be required.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Extreme imbalance (Combined ~64% of data) reduces power for pairwise comparisons involving smaller groups and may affect Type I error control.",
    "Outliers: Examine influence diagnostics (Cook's distance, leverage) given extreme max values in Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, and Average Speed."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For ANOVA-applicable continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Average Speed, AD if ANOVA used): Tukey's HSD for all pairwise comparisons, or Games-Howell if Welch's ANOVA used due to variance heterogeneity. Control family-wise error rate at α=0.05.",
    "For Path Efficiency (if Kruskal-Wallis used): Dunn's test with Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg correction.",
    "For Success (logistic regression): Pairwise odds ratios with Bonferroni-corrected confidence intervals, or marginal contrasts with Tukey adjustment.",
    "Planned contrasts: Compare multimodal (Combined) vs unimodal (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and vs Sham to test integration hypotheses.",
    "Effect sizes: Report η² for ANOVA, Cohen's d for pairwise comparisons, and odds ratios for Success."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Success: Sham expected to show substantially lower success rate (0.273) vs all active stimulation paradigms (0.673-0.785). Combined and Bright Visual Only expected highest success (~0.78-0.79).",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham expected slowest (4.68s), with Combined fastest (2.56s), followed by Bright Visual Only (2.61s). Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only intermediate (~3.05-3.14s).",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham lowest (0.308), Combined and Bright Visual Only highest (~0.50), Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only intermediate (~0.43-0.43).",
    "Average Speed: Sham slowest (10.74), Combined fastest (12.83), with modest differences across active paradigms (11.97-12.68).",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): Sham lowest (0.236, most directed), Combined highest (0.399, most variable), with visual-only and ICMS-only intermediate. Higher AD may indicate more exploratory behavior or less efficient path planning.",
    "Overall pattern: Combined stimulation appears to optimize performance across metrics; Sham clearly impaired; unimodal stimulations intermediate with subtle differences between visual and ICMS modalities."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe group size imbalance (Combined: 48846 vs Sham: 3505) reduces statistical power for Sham comparisons and may inflate variance estimates.",
    "Non-normal distributions (especially Path Efficiency, Time-to-Target) violate ANOVA assumptions; transformations or non-parametric alternatives required.",
    "Binary Success outcome makes ANOVA inappropriate; logistic regression necessary but interpretation differs from continuous outcomes.",
    "No repeated-measures structure modeled; treats all trials as independent despite multiple trials per mouse (8 mice, unequal trials per mouse). Mixed-effects models would better account for mouse-level clustering.",
    "No covariate adjustment (e.g., learning effects, trial number, session effects); temporal confounds possible.",
    "AD bounded on [0,1] with mean 0.38; standard ANOVA may produce predictions outside bounds.",
    "Extreme outliers present (e.g., Time-to-Target max=201s, Path Efficiency max=29.8) may disproportionately influence means and variances."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit mixed-effects models with random intercepts for Mouse to account for clustering, using appropriate distributions: linear mixed models for Time-to-Target (log-transformed), Average Speed, and AD (beta regression or transformed); generalized linear mixed model with binomial family for Success; and either robust regression or log-transformed linear mixed model for Path Efficiency. Include trial-level covariates (e.g., trial number, session) to control for learning. Conduct planned contrasts comparing Combined vs unimodal and vs Sham with Westfall adjustment for multiple comparisons."
}
